From 1e21270685ae4c14361dd501da62cdc4be867d4e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Keith Busch <kbusch@kernel.org>
Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2022 08:21:07 -0600
Subject: [PATCH] crypto: fix crc64 testmgr digest byte order

The result is set in little endian, so the expected digest needs to
be consistent for big endian machines.

Fixes: f3813f4b287e ("crypto: add rocksoft 64b crc guard tag framework")
Reported-by: Vasily Gorbik <gor@linux.ibm.com>
Reported-by: Corentin Labbe <clabbe.montjoie@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Keith Busch <kbusch@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220322142107.4581-1-kbusch@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

diff --git a/crypto/testmgr.h b/crypto/testmgr.h
index f1a22794c404..59919a636508 100644
--- a/crypto/testmgr.h
+++ b/crypto/testmgr.h
@@ -3686,11 +3686,11 @@ static const struct hash_testvec crc64_rocksoft_tv_template[] = {
 	{
 		.plaintext	= zeroes,
 		.psize		= 4096,
-		.digest		= (u8 *)(u64[]){ 0x6482d367eb22b64eull },
+		.digest         = "\x4e\xb6\x22\xeb\x67\xd3\x82\x64",
 	}, {
 		.plaintext	= ones,
 		.psize		= 4096,
-		.digest		= (u8 *)(u64[]){ 0xc0ddba7302eca3acull },
+		.digest         = "\xac\xa3\xec\x02\x73\xba\xdd\xc0",
 	}
 };
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `crypto/testmgr.h`**
   - The expected digest values for the CRC64 test vectors have been changed from a format that uses a `u64` array to a string literal format that represents the same values in little-endian byte order.
   - Specifically, the following changes were made:
     - The digest for the `zeroes` plaintext was changed from `(u8 *)(u64[]){ 0x6482d367eb22b64eull }` to `"\x4e\xb6\x22\xeb\x67\xd3\x82\x64"`.
     - The digest for the `ones` plaintext was changed from `(u8 *)(u64[]){ 0xc0ddba7302eca3acull }` to `"\xac\xa3\xec\x02\x73\xba\xdd\xc0"`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modifications in `crypto/testmgr.h` are directly related to ensuring that the expected digest values are consistent with the little-endian format used by the CRC64 implementation. This change addresses a bug that was reported regarding the digest byte order, particularly for big-endian machines. The patch corrects the expected output to match the actual output produced by the CRC64 algorithm, thereby fixing the inconsistency that could lead to incorrect test results.

Here is the commit message:
crypto: fix crc64 testmgr digest byte order

The result is set in little endian, so the expected digest needs to
be consistent for big endian machines.

Fixes: f3813f4b287e ("crypto: add rocksoft 64b crc guard tag framework")
Reported-by: Vasily Gorbik <gor@linux.ibm.com>
Reported-by: Corentin Labbe <clabbe.montjoie@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Keith Busch <kbusch@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220322142107.4581-1-kbusch@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by a mismatch in the expected digest byte order for the CRC64 test vectors, where the expected values were set in a format that did not account for the little-endian representation used by the CRC64 implementation. This inconsistency could lead to incorrect test results, especially on big-endian machines, as the expected output did not match the actual output generated by the algorithm.

 	}, {

-		.digest		= (u8 *)(u64[]){ 0xc0ddba7302eca3acull },
+		.digest         = "\xac\xa3\xec\x02\x73\xba\xdd\xc0",

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
.digest		= (u8 *)(u64[]){ 0x6482d367eb22b64eull },
.digest		= (u8 *)(u64[]){ 0xc0ddba7302eca3acull },
```
Reason:
The expected digest values were defined using a 64-bit unsigned integer in a format that assumes a little-endian representation. This caused a mismatch when the test was run on big-endian machines, leading to incorrect test results as the expected output did not match the actual output generated by the CRC64 algorithm.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
.digest         = "\x4e\xb6\x22\xeb\x67\xd3\x82\x64",
.digest         = "\xac\xa3\xec\x02\x73\xba\xdd\xc0",
```
Reason:
The patch changes the expected digest values to a byte string representation that explicitly defines the byte order in little-endian format. This ensures that the expected output is consistent with the actual output generated by the CRC64 implementation, thus resolving the issue on big-endian machines.
